1	# Home named in the window title
2	
3	For anyone with Prelude open next to other windows or tabs. Today the home page's window is called just "Prelude", the same as every other Prelude page, so in the taskbar, the tab strip or the browser's history you can't tell it's Home. Naming it "Home" lets people find their way back to the page that shows what needs them.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- The window (or browser tab) showing the home page is called "Home" instead of "Prelude".
8	- This is true however Home looks: with projects listed, on first run with no projects yet, when nothing is waiting, and when project names and paths are long.
9	- Nothing on the page itself changes: the heading, Needs you, the project cards and Open a project stay as they are.
10	
11	## Acceptance criteria
12	
13	- Going to the home page with projects open, the window's title reads "Home".
14	- On first run, with no projects yet, the window's title reads "Home".
15	- When nothing needs the person, the window's title still reads "Home".
16	- With very long project names and paths, the window's title still reads "Home", and the page looks as it does today.
17	- Coming back to Home from a project's page, the window's title changes back to "Home".
18	- After removing a project whose folder has gone, Home's window title still reads "Home".
19	
20	## Looks right in

1	# Landing Page - notes
2	
3	Prelude's home page (`/`), today `server/views/_home.eta`: an "Open a project"
4	form and a list of recent projects (name and path only). This design turns it
5	into a dashboard across the person's projects: "what needs me, and where was I?"
6	
7	Pages: `/` (Home), `/loading` (Home before its regions load; the design's way
8	to show it, not a URL the app needs), `/open` (the modal). States: typical,
9	first run (no projects), all caught up, long names.
10	
11	## Decisions
12	
13	- **Across projects** (the person's decision, 2026-10-16). Each project's own
14	  page keeps its full "In progress"; home gathers the parts that need action.
15	- **Needs you includes finished turns and questions** (the person, 2026-10-16),
16	  beside "ready to build", "build stopped" and "pull request open". Each row
17	  links to where it's answered; a pull request opens on the Git server.
18	  What's running right now stays in the bar, not repeated here.
19	- **Projects as a grid of cards** (a handful, the person said): each with its
20	  in-progress designs as links, how many things are waiting on you, and a line
21	  of facts (designs, stack, last change).
22	- **Regions load separately, with skeletons** (the person asked for loading
23	  states). The page arrives with the recent list (cheap); Needs you
24	  (`/home/needs-you`) and the projects' contents (`/home/projects`) each load
25	  into their own region. The projects show their real names and paths at once,
26	  with skeletons only for what's unknown. Each region shows a retry if it

3	- **R-n4v.** Needs you gathers what's waiting on the person from every recent project, newest first.
4	  *shown-on: /*
5	- **R-8hc.** A finished turn leaves Needs you once the person has opened its session, or after a week if they never do.

7	- **R-t7e.** Projects are listed by when something last changed in them, most recent first.
8	  *shown-on: /*
9	- **R-5ja.** The home page appears at once with the projects' names; what needs the person and what's in each project fill in as they're read, each on its own, so a slow one never holds up the rest.
10	  *shown-on: /loading*
11	- **R-p6r.** While the home page is open, what needs the person and what's in each project refresh on their own as soon as something changes in Prelude, and every five minutes for changes made elsewhere (not while the window is hidden).
12	- **R-h9b.** A recent project whose folder has gone stays listed, saying so, until the person removes it; removing it leaves the disk alone.
13	  *shown-on: /*
14	- **R-z3g.** The bar shows how many things are waiting on the person across all their projects, and leads home; it shows nothing when none are.
15	- **R-d0y.** If Prelude can't read part of the home page, that part says so and offers to try again, and the rest of the page still works.

1879

1890	`onNavigate(event)` sees every routing decision. `fetchContent` can be replaced
1891	with anything returning `{ url, ok, status, html }`, which is how the tests run
1892	a whole application against a table of canned responses - and `fetchFragment`,

1899	nothing at all — so this is decided rather than inherited:
1900	
1901	| | |

Home's window is now titled "Home". I couldn't run anything, so this is untested until Prelude's next render. One of the story's acceptance criteria isn't met yet (see below).

**What I changed**
- In `server/main.js`, `homePage` now passes the title "Home" for `/` instead of "Prelude". Two other cases that show the same page get it too: the page re-rendered when `POST /folders` is refused without script, and the redirect home after removing a project.
- `/loading` and `/open` still say "Prelude", because the story says to leave them alone. Their approved screens use different titles ("Home, while it loads" and "Open a project"), so a later change could match those.
- I added a section to `prelude/landing-page/NOTES.md` about this change and where the design and the story differ. `routes.json` already pointed at the app's views, `RULES.md` had no proposed rules, and no markup or styles changed.

**Please check before approving**
1. **The differences Prelude reported probably aren't Home's.** The render shows "Home · Prelude" and `/_prelude/…` stylesheets on every route, including `/loading` and `/open`. Both come from the design shell's head (`prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_head.eta`). The approved screens came from the app's own head (`server/views/_head.eta`), which shows the title as it is. I can't change the shell design, so if the next render still shows those lines, they come from the layout, not this port.
2. **One acceptance criterion isn't met:** "Coming back to Home from a project's page, the window's title changes back to Home." That works when Home loads as a whole page. It doesn't when Koda swaps Home into the current page, for example from the brand link or the Needs you link. Koda can't set the window title on a swap, and none of the app's other titled pages update it either. Fixing it means changing Koda or the app's layout, for every page, which is outside this change. I wrote this up in NOTES.md and didn't change the story.
